Q2: The Great Siege, shown by the chapter title '1779 — The Great Siege'. Camps and troops appear on the land north of the rock, and ships gather offshore from June 1779.
Q3: Not sure. The pictures never state a cause. I see ships blockading the bay and a land siege, and from Jan 1780 I see ships at sea and soldiers on a hillside. I would guess the hunger comes from a blockade or siege cutting off supplies, but nothing on screen says so.
Q4: Ships. Relief ships arrive in Jan 1780, Oct 1780 and April 1781, and they sail into the bay near the town. I am not certain, because nothing identifies them as a relief fleet.
Q5: A big naval attack on the rock, 11–14 Sep 1782. Many floating batteries line up in front of the rock and fight it through the day. At night they burn and explode, and the attack fails.
Q6: An airfield and runway are built in 1939 and extended into the sea in 1942–43. Over the years the sand also gets walls, fortifications, a few camps and houses, and finally a dense modern town and park (2015, 2026).
Q7: Not sure. The date counter shows 1969 (Jun and Aug 1969) with a wall or fence line across the sand north of the rock. Later frames show a small building there in 1973 and 1980, and by 1984 the area looks built up. The frames do not show a gate closing or reopening.
Q8: Not sure. The last frames show two towns, one on the rock and one on the sand to the north, with a shared runway and roads in 2026. Nothing explicitly shows a link such as a crossing, a road or workers commuting.

lost.why: The opening is dark night views with date counters and no explanation of what or where this is.
The intro flash-forwards (1411, 1782 attack, 1939) before the story starts, which is confusing.
The long run of near-identical empty-sand frames (1704–1734) never says what is happening or what is changing.
Soldiers appear on a hillside in Jan 1780 with no hint of who they are or why they are there.
A wall with cannons appears with no context.
A ruined town in 1782 is shown without saying why it is ruined or why people are hungry.
A street scene in 1910 appears with nothing to explain it.
1946–1984 is shown only as a few frames of sand, with no gate or border visible.
A street scene in 2026 appears with no sign of a border or a link between the towns.
The final recap jumps among 1735, 1943 and 2026 with no clear message.
